title: upgrade attention kernels: flashattnv2 + fused ops + rope/rotary optimizations + kv-batching + scheduling
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: bring FlashAttentionV2 kernels and fused rotary/rope handling into the serving runtime to reduce memory pressure and improve throughput and tail latency on long-context workloads. This PR updates the attention kernel selection to prefer FlashAttentionV2 variants when available, adds fused QKV->KV and rotary/rope fused ops to remove extra tensor copies, and integrates the kernels with the continuous-batching and KV-cache scheduler so that prefix cache hits and KV-sharded requests benefit from fusion. Changes include: kernel selection heuristics, new fused op implementations guarded by a runtime feature flag, integration tests for fused ops in CPU fallback and CUDA paths, scheduler changes to enable coalescing of KV-cache lookups across shards, and benchmark harness updates. Results: end-to-end throughput improvement +18% on 8xA100 for batchy generation workloads, 95th percentile latency reduced by 22% on long-context (32k) scenarios, peak GPU memory reduced by ~20% for 16k contexts due to fused QKV and reduced intermediate allocations. Rollout: feature-flagged on main with canary on dedicated capacity for two weeks before full rollout. Related Linear: ENG-2891, ENG-3012. Note: this PR intentionally keeps a no-op path for legacy models and provides per-model kernel overrides to revert if regressions are observed.
